utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further requests, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, at this stage are there any documents to tender, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. The documents we used have already been tendered through Ljubo Bojanovic and Mr. Butler. They're already in evidence, so there's no need.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. On the part of the Prosecution? No? Well, thank you. Well, Witness, thank you very much for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. Madam Usher will show you out of the room, and we all wish you a pleasant journey back home. You may go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, before we have the next witness, Mr. Stojanovic, how about next Monday and Tuesday? Do we have any witnesses on these two days?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On Monday, as you know, we don't have any witnesses because Mr. Vasic's statement will be according to 92 bis. And on Tuesday and Wednesday, according to the schedule, we are to hear Mr. Dragan Jokic, unless there are some changes. In any event, until the end of the day today, I'm going to inform you about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, could we hear Mr. Jokic next Monday, because next Monday, Tuesday we might have the full day, but on Wednesday, Thursday, or Friday, we may only have half day for, you know, the hearing because we will have the Plenary Meeting, you know, during that day. So my suggestion is that we should hear your witness as early as possible. You may discuss with your client during the break and inform us in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Could we have the next witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please make the solemn declaration in accordance with the paper Madam Usher is showing to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may sit down, please. Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Our witness is going to be led by Mr. Branko Lukic. So I would like to give the floor to my co-counsel, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I know that you are surprised every time when I get up. Examined by Mr. Lukic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, can you please tell us your full name.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: My name is Mihajlo Cvijetic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again for the record, could you spell your first and last name.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: M-i-h-a-j-l-o. My family name, C-v-i-j-e-t-i-c.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 28th of January, 1952, in Musici village in the Municipality of Kupres, in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us something about your educational background, where and when you finish the schools that you finished.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I finished elementary school in 1967 in Ravno village in the Municipality of Kupres in the Socialist Republic Bosnia and Herzegovina. I finished school for non-commissioned officers engineers in Karlovac in the Socialist Republic of Croatia. That was inform 1971. I completed the military academy of the land army in 1978 in Belgrade, in the Republic of Serbia. The General Staff school I completed in 1982 in Belgrade. I also attended a course on the implementation of the agreement in Prague, Oberammergau and Paris. I also attended a course for de-mining and instruction of explosives in Chatham, London, the United Kingdom. I also attended a course for de-mining and inspector for the control of de-mining in the organisation of Banja Luka. I believe this would be enough for the time being.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that it is more than enough. During your service in the army of Republika Srpska, what positions you held?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: During my service in the Republika Srpska army, I was the chief of engineers in a brigade. I was the inspector in the centre for verification, and I also performed the duties of the officer for mine clearance in the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you represent the entire army of Republika Srpska in your last position?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I represented the entire army of Republika Srpska, and I was in constant contact with the SFOR, with the representatives of SFOR, i.e., the representatives of the international organisations which are engaged in mine clearance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would kindly ask you to slow down a little so that our interpreters could catch up with you and interpret all your words properly.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we have already informed the Trial Chamber, you will be testifying about the situation in Bosnia and Herzegovina after the war. We would like you to provide us with your insight into character of Dragan Jokic. First of all, can you tell us: Since when have you known Dragan Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I have known Dragan Jokic since 1983, although I knew him even before because he also attended the military academy and that's where I saw him first. But since 1983, I have gotten to know him better, after our education that we did, that we went together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In our conversation, you described your activities and the activities of Dragan Jokic in the past date in Bosnia-Herzegovina by dividing them into three segments.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's correct. I divided those activities into three segments. I wanted to point to the activities pursuant to the implementation of the agreement according to Article 4, according -- Article 2, and the role of Mr. Dragan Jokic in the mine clearance of the areas in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The first segment would be the implementation of the accords falling under the regional control of arms, in other words, Article 4 of Annex 1. I would like to show you a document with this regard, and let me first ask you: The documents that we're going to show to you, can you tell us how did the Defence get -- got by those documents.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I brought these documents with me as I was preparing for this trial testimony, as when I was informed that I would appear before this Trial Chamber, I inspected all the documents. I wanted my testimony to be based on facts, on -- based on information and knowledge. I wanted to provide the best possible testimony, and that's why I brought these documents with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the usher assist us in showing the documents to the witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One of the documents that you have provided to the Defence will be shown to you. You gave this document to the Defence yesterday evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We apologise to the Trial Chamber and to our learned friends for the documents not being translated. I believe -- I hope we will appreciate that we only got hold of these documents yesterday evening, but we also hope that the witness will be able to provide us with the explanation of the contents and the importance of the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is the first time we've seen these documents. We could have seen them tomorrow night -- or last night. We could have some idea what they are. It is a bit absurd to be using documents that could have had some meaning and they, really, now have no meaning to us. But given that this is the last witness and given the subject matter, we will not object, but I just -- if there is any material for the next witness, we would please request that we get it in a timely manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I quite agree with you, and the -- I believe that any new-obtained documents should be furnished as soon as possible to the other party and to the Bench. Any pre-emptive attack is not allowed. But considering that those documents were not directly related to the critical period, that is the July 1995, and the witness will testify only on the character and the behaviours after the war of Mr. Jokic, we allowed the Defence to use those documents. But it should be a warning to the Defence team and in the future, if you have obtained any document, please furnish it to the other party. As a rule, the pre-emptive attack is not allowed. You may proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour. And as you could see, I wasn't sitting in the first session because I was photocopying these document at that time. So we really were not able to provide Your Honours and the Prosecution with these documents earlier than we did. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvijetic, please kindly tell us what the document that is before you is about.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dragan Jokic was engaged as an inspector of the control of armament which can be seen from the message 0717 to 126. Under 32 it says Dragan Jokic, male, born on 20 August 1957, and the identity card number is here. Such a list was sent to all the parties to the agreement, the verification centre of Croatia, the verification of Yugoslavia, and verification centre of the army of the federation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: If the witness could slow down just a little, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On receipt of this document, all the parties had the right to voice their objections to the document. Every party retains the right to exclude any other inspectors that are on the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Witness, I understand that you're eager to give your testimony, but whatever you said in this courtroom will be translated into the other two languages. So please make a pause after each sentence, and please speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Every party to the agreement received such a list of inspectors, and all the parties have the right to voice their objections to this list, which means that every person listed herein may be excluded from the list. The parties to the agreement did not have any objections to this list, which means they did not have any objections to Dragan Jokic's name on the list. So Mr. Jokic remained an inspector. This list was also submitted to the OSCE, and I wanted to show you the year 1996 on purpose, because, Your Honours, we believe that those were decisive years, very difficult years. And those were the years when human trades of the officers and the personnels who were engaged on this task could be seen best. Many things, many activities were not precisely regulated to the last letter. There was very little experience at the time. And that is why personal trades of individuals were so important. Mr. Jokic, while performing this activity, showed and proved himself, and he showed that the implementation of peace has no alternative in Bosnia. As a person, as a human being, he made his personal contribution towards the implementation of all the activities that were planned according to this article. Your Honours, there is an activity which is called escort. The escort team is the one that receives the team of inspectors of the other party. This is where Mr. Jokic was able --

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I am objecting to this, Your Honour, because it appears the witness is going into a very lengthy narrative without being asked any particular questions. I don't think that's proper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Lukic, I think you have to lead this witness, and the proceedings in this trial is in a pattern of question and answer. Maybe the witness is not familiar with this kind of practice. But you have to take the lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] We'll both do our best, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvijetic, your answers have to be a bit shorter, please. However, I will ask you to finish what you started.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I wanted to finish with Article 4, and I would like to say that Mr. Jokic's contribution was very correct when it comes to the activities according to Article 4.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any objections to his work by the parties who were informed about that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As far as the parties were concerned, as far as the places where we went to inspect, and as far as the parties who came to us to inspect, there were no objections.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second segment that we will be addressing is the implementation of the agreement on the measures for the building of understanding and peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In what capacity was Mr. Dragan Jokic engaged in this segment?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As for Mr. Jokic's activities in this area, he was active as an inspector. Secondly, he was active as a host during visits to bases.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the position of inspector of weapons control entail?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The position of inspector of verification of weapons meant that he had to be on the list of inspectors and had to go through the appropriate training courses either at home or abroad.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But what did the job consist in?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, he had to be in the inspection team and go to the other side. Or if he was in an escort team, he had to be the host, receive the teams from the other side and show them everything that was provided for in the protocol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a host, was he cooperative?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: As regards cooperativeness, the entire range of activity organised by Dragan Jokic's unit was done correctly and properly, both as regards the unit itself and the team of the other side, the inspection team.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were there any objections to Dragan Jokic's work in this area?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: No, there were no objections to Mr. Jokic's work in this area. And by your leave, by Their Honours' leave, I wish to say that it was very fortunate that Article 2 has been fully implemented in Bosnia-Herzegovina. This is something that gives me great satisfaction. This year, the full implementation will be completed, and this, of course, goes to the credit of all the people who participated in creating and implementing this article, and Mr. Jokic has played a role in all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the sake of the record, we have had D76/3 shown to the witness. I wish to ask Madam Usher to show the witness Exhibit D77/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, would you please assist us, because as you have heard, we have not had an opportunity to have this document translated for the benefit of the Court and the Prosecution. Could you tell us what this document is about.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, it's similar to the first document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a document like the first document we saw. It again contains a list of inspectors for the year 1997, and Mr. Jokic is under number 29, which means that he remained on the list of inspectors in the following year. And this means, of course, that there were no objections to his work. And this list was adopted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, what is the number of this document? It's 76 or 77?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The latest document the number is 77/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Your Honour, for clarity's sake, it appears to contradict the list. I think the list says 135/3. So I'm just wondering if perhaps we can have that clarified so that -- to avoid any future confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, to me it is 76/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I've been informed by the Court Deputy that this document should be 76/3. Let's stick to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid, Your Honour, that the previous document is 76. And also the confusion is created by correcting our numbers by the Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You know, the problem is that, you know, at this moment maybe we are not very much care about numbers, because you know, after this sitting -- or during the break the Court Deputy will discuss with the Defence counsel to give me the correct number. The problem is it is not translated into English, so we don't know actually which document it is. For instance, you know, in the list the witness told us that Mr. Jokic is number 26, and we could only check it according to the date of birth of this person. Otherwise, there is no other indications on that. This is the very, you know, problem we are facing. But anyway, you may go on and use the document. I think during the break we should have a correct numbering of all those documents so we know what you are talking about and what documents you are using. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And I believe the Prosecution now has corrected numbers. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvijetic, it is our mistake that we did not provide translations in time. Please don't worry about this yourself. I would now like to move on to the third topic we have to discuss today, and that is de-mining according to the standards of humanitarian de-mining. Has Mr. Dragan Jokic been involved in this type of work?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, when broaching this topic, allow me to say that the removal of mines and the de-mining of minefields is the most complex activity and the most high-risk activity, both for the person carrying out the de-mining and for the users of the de-mined area. In this case, referring to Mr. Dragan Jokic, I can state openly and with full responsibility that he personally invested a great deal of effort in carrying out these activities properly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Jokic participate in these activities from the very beginning?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will again mention the problem of the year 1996, when soldiers were suddenly dismissed so that engineers and officers were practically left on their own, and there was simply no other way but for an officer to take up an instrument, put on a helmet and personally work on removing mines so that the return of refugees could proceed according to plan. Mr. Jokic personally did this work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us what his personal involvement consisted in, in the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: With respect to his personal involvement, I will again refer to the complexity of the situation we found ourselves in. What I wish to say here is that Mr. Jokic took an instrument in his hand to feel for the mines, and he personally -- it was a kind of probe. And he personally took part in de-mining to ensure that it proceeded according to plan. All this took place in villages, hamlets, to which mostly Muslims were to return, the Muslim population. That was the situation. Jokic first did this personally, then he trained a group, and later on he did this in cooperation with SFOR. SFOR helped us to organise ourselves, and he took part in these activities then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Jokic take part in training de-mining personnel?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. As soon as the first training course was completed by SFOR we organised training in our units, and Mr. Jokic was in charge of this training. He selected commanders, komandirs, and people to work on de-mining. He selected them for this task.?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like to ask the usher to help us with the following document. The next document should be D79/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, what segment of Mr. Jokic's participation can we see in this document?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this document before us shows that Mr. Dragan Jokic, through his personal activity, made it possible for Captain Radenko Petrovic to take over the duty of komandir of a de-mining unit. And Mr. Dragan Jokic took on part of his job in order to help Lieutenant Dragan Simic. And we can see that from this document. Later on, during his later activities, we can see that this was a very helpful move.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're finished with this document. I would now like to ask Madam Usher to assist us with the next document, D85/3.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, I will ask you, first of all, what the harvest drive refers to.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, the harvest drive was organised by SFOR from time to time. It was a drive to gather explosive devices, mines, weapons, and other military equipment. The citizens would bring these items to the barracks. They would report them and hand them in. Every unit was duty-bound to receive these items, to take an inventory, to list them and to destroy them. The engineers were mostly active in destroying explosive devices and mines. We did this first, and then our colleagues from SFOR took over this duty, which made it easier for us to do the job.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic, I think this is not a good approach. My suggestion is that you read that document in B/C/S so the interpretation booth could have it translated into English, because this document is not very long. But it will help us to know where is that harvest thing, you know. Otherwise we are in total darkness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvijetic, would you be kind enough to read out for us this document so that Their Honours and the Prosecution can know what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: When I was preparing to testify here, I only wanted to show this as an example, as a kind of sample. There are many such documents. The zetva or harvest drivers were planned every three months, and then every six months, and then as things quieted down, once a year and so on. I have taken this document as an example, simply to remind us of all this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you please tell us who is sending the document to whom, and could you read out its content.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The command of the 503rd Motorised Brigade carried out a drive to gather equipment and materiel as part of the Zetva or harvest drive, and it is sending this document to the command of the 5th Corps, and it says: "In the period from the 16th of August, to the 23rd of August, 2002, as part of the 'Zetva' or harvest drive, from the MUP of Republika Srpska, public security sector in Zvornik, we received a certain amount of weapons and ammunition which we stored in the depot Glinica 1." Second paragraph: "Please find attached a list of the equipment and materiel collected in this period." And from this document, we can see that four anti-personnel mines were collected, four -- as the witness said, hand grenades. And this is what was destroyed in the brigade. This is what the brigade destroyed. This is the document I was commenting on. Your Honours, please take into account that this is only a random sample. I didn't follow this from the year 1996 because if I had, there would have been many more such documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We've finished with that document. I'm now going to show you another document which luckily everyone in the courtroom will be able to understand because it's the only document we have in English. Mr. Cvijetic, this is a document which you provided to Dragan Jokic's Defence team last night.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what it's about?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes. I am particularly happy that this is 1996, which was the most complex and difficult year in view of the activities that were ongoing, and Major Jokic was given this certificate of achievement from cooperation with his colleagues at the SFOR, and I think it speaks for itself and it confirms what I've already said in my testimony about him. Once again, let me repeat that the de-mining or doing away with mines is the most complex operation, and only somebody with - how shall I put this? - a strong will and a lot of knowledge can tackle this kind of task.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this is document number D80/3. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm now going to show you the next document. To save time, I'm just going to read the contents of the document. "Multinational Division (S), recognition or acknowledgement is given to team S/5/1. It's an award for exceptional results achieved in work on de-mining the -- on the de-mining campaign in the summer of 1998 accorded to the de-mining team. "Your excellent work has helped in the elimination of mines and resettlement of civilians in the area. Your efforts serve the honour of the unit -- are to the credit of the unit." It is the multinational division. S is Sever or north. To SFOR and to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Now, when it says that this was a team S/5/1, who is that? Who was that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was the team provided by the 503rd Brigade. It was the one in which Mr. Jokic worked, and it was through his endeavours that this team took part in the work on de-mining the surfaces which had been mined.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And for the record, it is document D91/3. [In English] And, Your Honour, is it a good time to have a break now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break and we will resume at 12.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I would like Madam Usher to help us with two more documents we'll hopefully understand.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I'm not sure if there was any translation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English? Can you hear the English?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Would you please repeat your question, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cvijetic, on the screen in front of you there is a photograph showing a group of soldiers. Could you please tell us, if you remember, where and when this photograph was taken and who you can recognise on it.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, on this photograph I recognise Mr. Jokic. He is next to the civilian, standing next to the civilian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have to show us on the ELMO and use your pointer, please.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: This is Mr. Jokic. Next -- that's Mr. Jokic. Then I also recognise Mr. Eric. And the others are colleagues from the army of federation or, rather, the army of the federation and our colleagues from SFOR working on the de-mining project. But I should particularly like to emphasise Mr. Eric here, because Mr. Jokic proposed that Mr. Eric could continue working on de-mining projects for the coming period, and that's what happened next. He was a younger officer. He was a lieutenant colonel at the time. A 2nd lieutenant, actually. But otherwise this is a group photograph of people working on the de-mining project as a momentum [as interpreted] for us, and Mr. Jokic, and everyone else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just briefly let's see the second set of photographs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you have to ask a question when this picture was taken and where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I did, Your Honour, but I don't think I got a response, so I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, please. For the sake of the record, please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Cvijetic, do you happen to remember where and when the photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly. I think it was -- I can't remember exactly. It was at the beginning, so I can't tell you exactly, I'm afraid, but I think it was in Doboj or -- just a moment, please. Just give me a second. No, I'm sorry, I can't give you an exact answer to give you a time frame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the time?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Well, roughly speaking, this is 1997. 1997 is the year.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's take a look at these other photographs.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: These photographs here, I can recognise Mr. Jokic, the OSCE representative, OSCE. So it was cooperation there, an instance of cooperation. A colonel of the Swiss army on this side here. I can recognise him. It was a long time ago. And Mr. Jokic. They're sitting there together. Then the representative of the multinational division north and Mr. Jokic. And here we have the inspectors and Mr. Jokic with them. Here we have an exchange of gifts with the representative of the army of the federation, probably when they were visiting the base. And here once again we have him with the representative of the multinational division north, him and Mr. Jokic. So all these photographs testify to a very proper and concrete form of cooperation, concrete and proper cooperation with representatives of the SFOR, with representatives of international organisations with the aim of timely and professional de-mining.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And for the record, these were exhibits, Defence Exhibits D82/3-1 and D81/3-2. The usher will now give you another document to look at, and I'm going to ask you whether the execution of tasks given -- that you had after the war that Mr. Jokic took part in, were they easy and simple tasks that you were given to carry out? Tell us first whether they were simple, whether it was easy to carry out the assignments that you had given before you. Or were there many obstacles?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have a document here which speaks about the implementation of the Dayton Accords and the attending documents, where the command of the 5th Corps conducted an analysis, and in the frameworks of that analysis mention is made of certain problems -- and I should especially like to stress that this was done in 1999. That was the date when they speak about major problems. In continuation of the document, it says problems occurring during inspection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please tell us briefly, looking through the document which is Defence Exhibit D83/3, what kind of problems you encountered. What does it say in the document dated 1999?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Mr. President, in this document the problems that occurred when we conducted inspection, that is to say three years later, there were large quantities of ammunition in -- not in their original wrapping. A lot of bulk ammunition not in its own original wrapping and casing. So to establish what the situation was, we had to spend a great deal of time in sizing up the situation, and it required, I would say, a lot of courage too. Then we didn't have enough warehouse space and the proper warehouse space for storing this materiel and making a list of what we stored, keeping records, and lack of training on the part of those handling the materiel and equipment. So first of all to see what materiel there was, to record the materiel, the lack of necessary documentation pertaining to the materiel equipment, and the keeping of records in three types of records. We had the SFOR records, the OSCE records, and the Military Accountancy Centre of Banja Luka, their records. So three sets of records. I don't want to go into the different problems of the different areas of activity, but I'd just like to focus on those three aspects. A large number of materiel and equipment; not the proper storage space; and not enough training of personnel, not enough professional people to deal with the situation. So all these problems had to be addressed, and each of the units had its assignments to perform in that regard, and Mr. Jokic did too. Mr. Jokic worked with his unit on matters of this kind, because in view of the fact that the engineers had to do with the bulk of the work related to mines and de-mining and ammunition and so on, both to test its operational use, the quantity and storing such materiel and equipment too. And I should once again like to emphasise that this was three years later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in that connection let me ask you this: The situation in 1996 and 1997, was it worse or not? Worse or better?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: The situation was incalculably worse in the terms of pointers stipulated here. So at that time we had a lot of material dispersed over a large area, and we had to locate all this materiel and devices and to make records of it and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Cvijetic. These are our questions of you. I don't know if Mr. Karnavas will have some questions of you, and after that I would ask you to kindly answer the questions put to you by our learned friends and the Trial Chamber. Thank you very much?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Karnavas, do you have any questions to be put to this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I may have one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Cross-examined by Mr. Karnavas:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We haven't met or spoken, but let me ask you whether you know Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, sir, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We understand that he was an engineer by training in the military. My question to you is: During this critical period of time that you've been testifying, that is after the Dayton Accords, do you know whether Mr. Blagojevic participated with the international community, international forces, in events such as the de-mining, events that you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He was a member of the initial conference that held -- that was held in Vienna in 1996. And from then on, from that meeting on, Mr. Blagojevic planned, managed and organised the system of de-mining in the army of Republika Srpska, and he also cooperated with the army of the federation, the SFOR and other international organisations. His cooperation was very correct, very good, very rich. And this was a very fruitful period in the life of Colonel Blagojevic in that area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: Yes. Good afternoon, Your Honours. I do have a few questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, please. Cross-examined by Ms. Issa:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. I just have a couple of questions, sir. You're not aware of Mr. Jokic ever telling anyone where the victims of the Srebrenica massacre were or the location of the mass graves, are you?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: Did he ever tell anybody? I'm afraid I didn't understand your question. Could you please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he say anything at all about identifying the location of the mass graves? Did he assist in any way to do that, to the international forces?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know if he ever said that to anybody. And he never said it to me personally, and -- I'm not aware of that. Whether he said it to anybody else, I really wouldn't be able to tell you anything to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And by the same token, sir, I take it that you're not aware of Mr. Blagojevic ever assisting international forces with identifying the location of the mass graves, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. It calls for speculation, and she needs to lay a foundation which we don't have any in any way that Mr. Blagojevic was ever involved in any of these activities. So if she can lay a foundation then she can ask the question, but the question assumes a fact that's not in evidence, as it's posed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe that witness can answer the question whether it's yes or no, just like he answered the question that was put to Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I'm a Bosnian. You have to repeat your question at least twice. I hail from Bosnia, and that's what you have to do with us Bosnians. So can you please repeat the question that referred to Mr. Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I will do that. Do you know whether Colonel Blagojevic ever assisted international forces in locating the mass graves?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: I really don't know whether it was ever asked from Colonel Blagojevic, whether anybody asked Colonel Blagojevic to do that. I really don't know if anybody requested that from Colonel Blagojevic. If anybody had, I'm sure that he would share any information that he might have had with the person that requested it. I know Blagojevic very well, and I'm sure he would have done that. I don't know whether anybody asked that of him. I can't say yes or no. In any case, if anybody had asked him to share that information, I'm sure he would have shared it, had he known where that was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. During the period of 1996 and 1997, did you know that Mr. Obrenovic and Mr. Jokic were -- got into trouble or were caught for hiding ammunition from SFOR? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MIHAJLO CVIJETIC
utterances.text: You know what? I have presented information here, and I've told you about the problems that we encountered in the course of our work. For example, SFOR comes today and inspects your weapons. Overnight a certain quantity of weapons is found somewhere else and a peasant brings it to you, and you face a problem because the duty operations officer doesn't report it, and when the inspection returns, this becomes a problem. In any case, I'm not aware of any problems involving the hiding of weapons. I believe that this cooperation was always correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to let the witness answer the question, but I think that it would be fair toward the witness to tell him who said something, or what was the evidence, or to lay some kind of foundation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well -- but anyway, the witness answered that he was not aware of any problems involving the hiding of the weapons. So it's over. But if the witness answered the other way, I believe that is the responsibility for the Prosecutor to present some evidence. I think this matter is answered. Yes, Ms. Issa.

utterances.speaker: MS. ISSA
utterances.text: I don't have any further questions, Your Honour, but perhaps to assist, Ms. Sinatra was actually the person who posed those questions to Mr. Obrenovic and that's where we got that from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any redirect?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. At this stage are there any documents to tender? Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, and we believe that the Prosecution won't be able to say whether they object or no. It would probably be subject to translation. But we would like to tender these documents we used today, and those are numbers D76/3, D77/3, D78/3 -- sorry, 79/3, D80/3 D81/3, D82/3, D82/3 and D85/3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have no objection to those being used -- dealt with the same way the ones I think yesterday, that they provisionally be allowed, and if we have any problems, we'll let the Court know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. But document D80/3 is written in English. It's a certification, as well as the document D82/3-1 and -2. Those are two photos. So at this stage we could make a decision on those two documents. They are admitted into evidence. As for the other evidence, I'm afraid we cannot admit them at this moment, but later on if we see the translation I believe that we will consider those documents' admission at that time. Thank you. So decided. Well, Witness, thank you very much indeed for coming to The Hague to give your evidence. We wish you a pleasant journey back home. Madam Usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. And if you will allow me, would like to say a sentence. I would kindly ask this Tribunal to address the issue of de-mining and to use its reputation with certain institutions that might have a say in the legal regulation of this problem. I myself have been a victim of a mine, and I know what it looks like when a mine is laid and what happens when somebody is hurt by a mine. So I would kindly ask you if you could raise this issue with the authorities to give it the proper legality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may go now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we booked this courtroom until 7.00 today, and we finished the witness before 1.00. At this stage, are there any other matters that the parties would like to raise? Yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Karnavas and I can argue for the next six hours if you like, but you probably don't want to hear us. Mr. Stojanovic and I were able to talk about the expert report of the witness yesterday. And we did actually take Mr. Karnavas's idea and we did keep the basics of the report and I believe agreed on areas that would not be in. So that, I think, should be resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. I think if, Mr. Stojanovic, you could submit that redacted, if I say, redacted report we will have it admitted into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Yesterday, we had a long meeting, and we discussed the expert report in depth, and we agreed on the contents of the report. Our associate Dragoslav Djukic has prepared that, and as soon as this session is finished we're going to provide the Prosecutor with the redacted report in B/C/S and in English, and after that we're going to also provide it to the Trial Chamber with our proposal for this redacted report to be admitted into evidence as a Defence exhibit. And this also refers to the translation of the rules of service and the instruction on the work of commands that we tendered into evidence yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. McCloskey? You must have some clarifications; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I believe Mr. Stojanovic may have one other announcement, and I would see what he had to say first before I ask the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'm convinced that Mr. McCloskey could not argue with me for six hours. Maybe this is just throwing the ball into my part of the courtyard. I just wanted to inform you that with today's day and with this last witness we have finished the presentation of Defence exhibits. And we would like to inform that during the last break we have finally been authorised to inform you that Dragan Jokic, for the reasons for the security of his son, primarily, does not want to testify on his behalf, and I would kindly ask you to make a note of that. We are not going to have any evidence to present next week before this Trial Chamber. In any case, thank you for the time that you were willing to give us. We have tried to use that time rationally and effectively with our witnesses in the best intention to help our client. So this brings the Defence case officially to an end.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As I said before that we fully respect the free will of your client. Whatever decisions he makes, we'll respect it. Thank you. Could we go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, it seems to me that there is nothing else on the agenda, and I'm very glad to say that we finished the Defence case of Mr. Jokic ahead of time, and I understand there are some leftover housekeeping matters to deal with, especially concerning some documents which has not been admitted into evidence. I hope the parties will make submissions before the end of the whole case so that we could consider the admission of those documents in due time. I would like to repeat that if any party have the rebuttal or rejoinder case or reopening his case, they could file us before the 26th of August so that we could be prepared for any hearing -- possible hearings in the future. I believe that's all I have to say. If there is nothing else the parties would like to raise at this stage, we declare the hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 1st day of September, 2004

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.30 p.m.,
